content: Rosuvastatin is prescribed to help reduce the levels of cholesterol and other fatty substances in the blood when combined with lifestyle changes such as a healthy diet, weight loss, and regular exercise. Cholesterol is a fat-like substance that can accumulate along the walls of blood vessels, leading to a condition called atherosclerosis. This buildup can restrict blood flow and reduce the oxygen supply to vital organs like the heart and brain. By lowering cholesterol and fat levels in the blood, rosuvastatin can help reduce the risk of developing heart disease, angina (chest pain), strokes, and heart attacks. Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medications known as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, or statins. It works by slowing down the production of cholesterol in the body. In addition to taking this medication, adopting certain lifestyle changes, such as eating a diet low in saturated fat and cholesterol, exercising for at least 30 minutes on most days, and losing weight if overweight, can further help lower cholesterol levels. Rosuvastatin is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once daily, with or without food. It is important to take it at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without increasing or decreasing the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. Your doctor will likely start you on a low dose and gradually increase it, usually no more than once every 2 to 4 weeks. Continue taking rosuvastatin even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking rosuvastatin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to rosuvastatin or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention anticoagulants (blood thinners) like warfarin, cimetidine, cyclosporine, ketoconazole, other cholesterol-lowering medications (e.g., clofibrate, fenofibrate, gemfibrozil, niacin), and spironolactone. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. If you are taking aluminum and magnesium hydroxide antacids, take them at least two hours after rosuvastatin. Inform your doctor if you have liver disease, as you may be advised not to take rosuvastatin. Additionally, let your doctor know if you consume large amounts of alcohol or have a history of liver, kidney, or thyroid disease. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor immediately, as rosuvastatin can harm the fetus. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking rosuvastatin. Ask your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while on this medication, as alcohol can increase the risk of serious side effects. Follow a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet while taking rosuvastatin. This diet should include foods like cottage cheese, fat-free milk, fish (not canned in oil), vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils and margarines (e.g., corn, safflower, canola, and soybean oils). Avoid foods high in fat, such as fatty meats, liver, egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, shortening, lard, pastries, cakes, cookies, gravy, peanut butter, chocolate, olives, potato chips, coconut, cheese (other than cottage cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, and fried foods. If you miss a dose of rosuvastatin, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Rosuvastatin may cause side effects. Mild side effects include constipation, heartburn, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, depression, joint pain, and cough. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects are rare but require immediate medical attention. These include muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness; lack of energy; fever; chest pain; yellowing of the skin or eyes; pain in the upper right abdomen; nausea; extreme tiredness; unusual bleeding or bruising; loss of appetite; flu-like symptoms; sore throat, chills, or signs of infection; rash; hives; itching; difficulty breathing or swallowing; swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; and numbness or tingling in the fingers or toes. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store rosuvastatin in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order tests to monitor your body’s response to rosuvastatin. Inform your doctor and laboratory personnel that you are taking this medication before undergoing any tests. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
